Store final class

JSONL-backed heartbeat store. One file per day under the data dir — $XDG_DATA_HOME/candy-codetime/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl (fallback ~/.local/share/candy-codetime/, resolved by self::defaultDir()) — the path stays appendable, every editor plugin just >> echoes a JSON line; whatever loose modes such a line is minted with are swept back to owner-private by self::enforcePrivateModes() on the next CLI launch.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly string $dir, public readonly int $rangeBeatBudget = self::MAX_RANGE_BEATS)
static clampRangeDays(int $days): intClamp a requested day count to [1, MAX_RANGE_DAYS] so an out-of-range value from the CLI cannot drive loadRange() into an unbounded walk.
static defaultDir(): stringDefault per-user directory (XDG / fallback to ~).
static ensurePrivateDir(string $dir, string $label = 'data directory'): voidCreate (or tighten) the data directory to owner-private 0700.
static ensurePrivateFile(string $path, string $label = 'data file'): voidTighten an existing file to owner-private 0600, throwing when the chmod fails. Public because AutoBackup must apply the same law to the copies it writes: a byte-for-byte clone of a private day file, left at the umask default, leaks the same paths (as supplied) one directory over.
enforcePrivateModes(): voidRe-establish the whole privacy contract, not just the paths this process writes. A plugin that direct-appends with >> runs no candy-codetime code at all, and a pre-rename migration merely moves the tree — files minted that way can sit at the shell's umask, world- readable absolute paths and project maps. The sweep tightens the data directory (0700), every day file and archived day file (0600), and the SQLite database with its -wal/-shm sidecars (0600). It runs on every CLI launch — reads included — so any exposure lasts at most until the tool is run next, and it throws on an unfixable mode exactly like the write paths do.
countMatched(callable $drops): intCount beats the forget door would remove (CT-S42). Lines that do not parse are never counted: a beat whose identity cannot be proven is a beat that survives. Reading populates the day cache, so callers that stop at the count must invalidate() before reading again (the CLI forget arm does).
forget(callable $drops): intRewrite every day file excluding the beats the door matches (CT-S42).
silenceDiagnostics(): voidStop the store writing to stderr; counting continues (CT-S19). The dashboard launcher calls this the moment the alt screen takes over, so mid-session reloads can never spray raw bytes into a sync frame.
drainDiagnostics(): arrayTake the data-loss counters since the last drain (CT-S19). Resetting here is what makes a footer count describe the load it accompanies instead of the whole process lifetime.
loadDay(\DateTimeImmutable $day): array
loadRange(\DateTimeImmutable $from, \DateTimeImmutable $to): arrayLoad every heartbeat in [$from, $to] — date range inclusive.
invalidate(): voidInvalidate the day cache (forces reload on next loadDay).
append(Heartbeat $hb, ?CancellationToken $token = null, int $lockTimeoutMs = self::APPEND_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS): voidAppend a heartbeat to today's JSONL file.
hasAnyHeartbeat(): boolCT-S46: any non-empty day file answers yes without parsing contents.

SugarCraft\CodeTime\Backup

AutoBackup final class

Rotating backup manager for JSONL data files. Archives (copies) files whose mtime has aged past the keepDays threshold. Scope of the copy-only rotate() is the per-day *.jsonl files; a byte copy of a live SQLite database would be a torn snapshot at best, so the database gets its own door instead: archiveSqliteDatabase() runs VACUUM INTO, which snapshots consistently from a live connection (the CLI's plain backup still refuses to copy the .db and says why).

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly string $backupDir, private readonly array $dirs = [])
rotate(int $keepDays = 30): intArchive day files older than keepDays (copy-only — nothing is ever deleted from the data directory; the "rotating" in the class name is an archive cadence, not a retention sweeper).
archiveSqliteDatabase(string $dbPath): stringCrash-safe archive /** Crash-safe archive of the SQLite database via VACUUM INTO.
listBackups(): array

A rule file (.sugartrackignore / .sugartrackallow) larger than the declared byte ceiling. A dedicated type (CT-S39, finding 059) so the CLI reports it as the opt-out misconfiguration it is — never wrapped in the storage-error envelope, which would tell the user their disk failed when their config file was refused on size.

SugarTrackIgnore final class

Loads .sugartrackignore glob patterns and matches file paths.

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly array $patterns = [])
static load(string $path, string $label = 'ignore file'): selfLoad patterns from an ignore file.
patternCount(): intNumber of active patterns (comments and blank lines excluded).
hasWholesalePattern(): boolTrue when some pattern is wildcard-only — it ignores EVERY path the matcher is ever consulted about.
isIgnored(string $path): boolReturns true if the file path should be ignored.
isAllowed(string $path): boolThe sibling control of isIgnored, for ".sugartrackallow" files: the same three-leg match, read as a rescue instead of a rejection. The CLI consults an allow-list FIRST — a path matched here is tracked without the deny file ever being consulted — so the two files together give first-match precedence to the allow side (upstream .takatrack parity, finding 045).

HeartbeatReader interface

The read contract the dashboard and the export/gaps report paths need.

MethodSummary
loadRange(\DateTimeImmutable $from, \DateTimeImmutable $to): arrayLoad every heartbeat in [$from, $to] — date range inclusive.
invalidate(): voidDrop any cached reads so the next load sees what is on disk now.
hasAnyHeartbeat(): boolDoes this store hold ANY heartbeat at all, anywhere (CT-S46)? The dashboard swaps its panes for a getting-started block exactly when the answer is no — a first-run user must see the next action, not three politely empty frames. Distinct from an empty WINDOW: old records elsewhere keep the normal panes.

SqliteBackend final class

SQLite-backed heartbeat + milestone store. Provides an alternative to the JSONL store with query capabilities, and satisfies the same HeartbeatReader contract, so dashboard can read it exactly like push/export/gaps already do.

invalidate(): voidNo cached reads exist over the live database, so there is nothing to drop — the honest no-op the HeartbeatReader contract expects (same method Store uses to re-read its day files after r).

Detect final class

MethodSummary
static language(string $file): stringThe language an extension names; 'unknown' when the map is silent.
static project(string $file, string|false|null $cwd): stringThe repository the file belongs to: the nearest ancestor carrying a .git (directory or file — worktrees use the file form), else the first segment of the path relative to the working directory (the directory itself when the file sits in it), else 'unknown'. An unrelated absolute path's first segment is filesystem geography, not a project name, so it never becomes a label.
